info.name: Crumb & Co. — Backend API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the Crumb & Co. e-commerce backend (Express v5 + Prisma).

## Setup
1. Start the server: `npm run dev` (defaults to http://localhost:4000).
2. Seed the database: `npm run db:seed` (creates the admin `admin@crumbco.dev` / `Admin123!`, products).
3. Import the environment `crumb-and-co.environment.json` and select it.

## How to run
- Run the whole collection in order (Auth → Me → Users → Categories → Products → Cart → Orders → Cleanup).
- Tokens are captured automatically: Login requests store the JWT in the environment variable `accessToken` / `adminAccessToken`, which every protected request reads.
- Refresh tokens are httpOnly cookies handled automatically by Postman's cookie jar.
- Re-running: Register requests require a fresh email (a 409 duplicate will fail the test) — clear the email variables in the environment or use new ones to re-run. Product creation tolerates 409 and reuses the seeded product captured from the list endpoints.

## Auth model
- Register/login → access JWT (Bearer). Refresh token delivered via httpOnly cookie on `/api/v1/auth`.
- Admin endpoints require the seeded admin (or any user promoted via PATCH /users/:id/role).
- Customers can delete their own account via DELETE /me (hard delete; order history is detached and kept). Admin accounts cannot delete themselves.
- Mock payment provider auto-marks orders PAID.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register, login, refresh, logout. Tokens are saved to environment variables for downstream requests.

item.name: Register Managed User
item.description: Second account used by the admin-management tests in the Users folder. On re-runs this 409s (already registered) — the id is captured reliably by the following Login Managed User request.

item.name: Login Managed User
item.description: Always returns the managed user's id (even on re-runs when registration 409s), so `managedUserId` is reliably set for the Users folder.

item.name: Login Admin
item.description: Uses the seeded admin (see `npm run db:seed`).

item.name: Refresh
item.description: Reads the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie automatically. Rotates the session and returns a fresh access token.

item.description: Tries to move the paid order back to PENDING, which is not a valid transition from PAID or PROCESSING.

item.description: Checkout with a product that does not exist returns HTTP 400 with code NOT_FOUND.

item.name: Checkout — empty cart (409)
item.description: Authenticated checkout without items while the cart is empty → conflict. (Cart was cleared by the happy-path checkout.)
